methods.experiment: Prior experimental context reports a sine generator setting of 1 Vpp; photos are setup references. For added IM_39-45, only the nominal frequency/file mapping is confirmed; generator amplitude and other acquisition conditions are unverified. No measured transducer input or acoustic reference.
methods.units: Time_us * 1e-6 relative to first timestamp; IM Data28 counts; accel Raw_Z converted to g using each recording full scale and nominal ASM330LHH sensitivity (2/4/8/16 g: 0.000061/0.000122/0.000244/0.000488 g/count); no individual calibration. Original CSV unchanged; raw_counts retained in loaded record.
methods.timing: Half-open [start,end) windows. Nominal schedules begin at configured start_s, not inferred switches. Explicit bounds override schedule; trim follows bounds. Frequency selection is applied AFTER complete schedule construction.
methods.support: Requested window must be within recording; at record end allow exactly one full-record mean sample interval plus floating tolerance for conventional half-open support. Actual first/last samples and use of tolerance reported; no silent shortening.
methods.sampling: Reject nonfinite/duplicate/decreasing timestamps. Estimate fs=(N-1)/(last-first) per retained window. Interpolate linearly to N equispaced times; no clock correction from targets.
methods.fft: Remove uniform-signal mean; periodic Hann; no additional filters. Global argmax over every positive rFFT bin through Nyquist when present; exclude DC only. Targets never restrict search.
methods.amplitude: One-sided sinusoidal peak amplitude 2*abs(FFT)/sum(window), except DC and exact Nyquist not doubled. Native/padded transform lengths differ; normalization always original window sum. Dominant peak need not be excitation fundamental.
methods.interpolation: Configured interpolation_points actual adjacent bins around global maximum (default 3, optional 5; both counts additionally retained in the explicit seven-method comparison); unweighted degree-2 least-squares fit in centered bin offsets and configured log or linear amplitude. Five bins are k-2 through k+2; three-bin mode retains the original closed form. Vertex delta=-b/(2*a), frequency=f[k]+delta*df; amplitude=q(delta) or exp(q(delta)). No fallback to fewer points. Reject tied maximum, unavailable neighbor, nonpositive/invalid values, nonconcavity, or vertex beyond half-bin. Native and padded spectra select their maxima independently.
methods.zero_padding: nfft=pad_factor*N; refine sampled spectrum only. Report native_df=fs/N, padded_df=fs/nfft, Hann ENBW=fs*sum(w**2)/sum(w)**2; these are not interchangeable with physical resolution.
methods.raw_metrics: raw_rms=sqrt(mean((raw-mean(raw))**2)); raw_rms_including_dc separate; raw_peak_to_peak=max(raw)-min(raw). Original retained samples, no trimming of outliers.
methods.noise: Each stated noise control kept separate; full file by default. Same one-sided Hann periodogram PSD abs(FFT)**2/(fs*sum(w**2)), double interior positive bins. PSD in each sensor output unit squared/Hz (IM counts^2/Hz; accel g^2/Hz), not amplitude. Original noise PSD/RMS retained. Supplemental nominal-band SNR uses the explicitly configured independent controls; no detection limit, responsivity or sensitivity calculated.
methods.quality: Boundary coverage failures always suppress FFT. Internal gap > max_gap_over_median remains a strict gap-check failure; default diagnostic mode also computes the same explicitly flagged linearly interpolated FFT. strict_global_* columns retain the strict result; fft_computed is computational availability, fft_valid is legacy strict gap eligibility, neither guarantees calibrated accuracy. Ratio comparison tolerance=max(1e-9,abs(threshold)*1e-9) handles exact-threshold floating error. Gap count, duration sum and duration fraction recorded; these do not assert lost samples. Raw extrema occupancy is diagnostic only and does not establish ADC/sensor saturation. Jitter, cycles, sampling margin, excursions and target mismatch remain flagged.
methods.sensitivity: Additional symmetric sweep trims and raw-order FFT at the same estimated fs; diagnostics of window and interpolation dependence, not independent repeats or alternative primary results.
methods.resolution: Independent record-level estimates grouped by base,target,window,method; arithmetic mean of finite estimates, sample SD(ddof=1) only n>=2. Computed and strict-gap views saved separately; flagged finite estimates retained in computed view with strict counts. Differences of group means are descriptive, not synchronized or calibrated two-tone resolution.
methods.target_diagnostics: Supplement only: maximum bin inside target +/- min(0.4*target,max(3*native_df,0.15*target)), unless explicit halfwidth. Minimum0.1Hz by default. Native/padded fits using the configured interpolation_points match selected bins; no replacement if boundary/nonlocal/invalid. Rank interpolated interior local maxima above minimum and below Nyquist; all noise/sidelobes retained, exact ties share rank. Rankings and relative amplitude are not SNR. Primary global peaks never change.
methods.volume: Selected files, target frequencies, levels, windows and pairing confirmation are recorded in effective CONFIG. Plot numeric volume ascending10to15; original segment order preserved. Each primary window is split into contiguous configured-duration subwindows (defaults: central20s, subwindows5s; effective values in parameters.json); not repeats. FFT amplitude, raw RMS, raw peak-to-peak remain distinct.
methods.volume_reference: Explicit file pairs joined by volume only. Normalize each sensor to its own configured reference-level amplitude (default volume10). Plot IM amplitude vs accel amplitude and Data28 counts/g ratio; not calibrated responsivity or a synchronized transfer function. Preserve all points and mark accel repeated-extrema occupancy at or above the configured threshold (default1%); usable descriptive ratio excludes flagged plateaus, unavailable FFT/amplitude, unequal targets or incompatible dominant frequencies. Timing warnings remain. User confirmation records condition matching, not simultaneous sampling.
methods.cross_sensor: User-confirmed condition-matched volume references are compared at whole-window level; no synchronized phases/coherence/transfer function, no pulse-to-pulse ratios, no physical calibration. Accelerometer sweep disabled by request.
methods.snr: Supplemental noise-control-referenced nominal-band excess-power SNR; default nominal +/-1Hz. Excited native Hann PSD integrated in the same exact physical band as the separate control's Welch PSD, clipped to common represented frequency support. Noise Welch: configured6s periodicHann,50%overlap,constant detrend,linear-power mean,no padding; too-short/unavailable controls not silently shortened. Piecewise-linear trapezoidal PSD integration including boundary interpolation; DC endpoint retained after detrending when the band reaches0Hz. Pexcess=Pexcited-Pnoise; SNRlinear=Pexcess/Pnoise, SNRdB=10log10(SNRlinear). Nonpositive excess gives NaN SNR and explicit status; measured Pexcited/Pnoise retained separately. No cross-control averaging, errorbars or automatic detection claim. Assumes independent control represents additive uncorrelated background during driven recording; IM_1 excess includes amplifier-added noise. Nearby interference also contributes. Original global FFT selection is unchanged. All effective windows/bands/df/ENBW/segment counts and timing flags recorded in SNR CSV and parameters.json. Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.signal.welch.html
methods.selected_view: Additional sweep/SNR plots use plots.sweep_view (default>=10Hz), selecting already-computed rows by nominal frequency. Complete plots and original acquisition time mapping remain; no recalculation or alternative peak search.
methods.figures: Main spectrogram restored to linear frequency0..Nyquist, viridis,100dB below max,2s Hann75%overlap; configurable. Cyan dots at nominal segment midpoints annotate desired frequencies, not peak estimates. Both linear/log frequency-axis versions use identical PSD and color limits. RMS/peak-to-peak amplitude panels use log axes; global-vs-target amplitudes explicitly distinguished. Resolution per-record spectra normalized to each own maximum INSIDE display crop for shape comparison only; numerical amplitudes unchanged. Resolution categorical method x-axis and mHz offset from base expose every repeat. Interpolation demo uses actual global-maximum native bin plus the configured symmetric neighborhood (default one neighbor on each side). Volume plots sort numeric levels ascending, never shift segment mapping. Plot settings below describe defaults; effective plot/FFT settings are recorded in parameters.json. Raw min/max envelopes in time bins of width max(0.02s,record_span/6000); spectrogram linearly interpolates N points between first/last record timestamps, fs=(N-1)/span, 2s periodic Hann (capped to record), configured75% overlap, constant detrend, one-sided PSD, dB relative to 1 unit^2/Hz, color range100dB below max. Spectrogram across internal gaps is explicitly labeled diagnostic by default; strict mode omits it. Dense spectrum displays keep the exact maximum in each of at most 6000 contiguous log-index buckets; peak selection and all numerical estimates use every FFT bin. Volume waveform figures show central three nominal cycles (capped at 2s), raw samples unchanged. Full positive spectra for each window; resolution zoom changes display only.
methods.primary_frequency_estimator: global_padded_3point; not selected by proximity to nominal
methods.largest_fft: Actual global argmax over all positive native rFFT bins, excluding DC; preserved as global_bin_hz. global_padded_hz repeats the full search on the padded grid.
methods.fft_comparison: Compute both three-point and five-point unweighted quadratic fits on the same native and padded Hann amplitude spectra, in the configured log/linear domain; retain all results and rejection statuses. Existing global_parabolic aliases use configured interpolation_points (default 3).
methods.sine_fit: Unweighted variable-projection least squares of c+a*cos(2*pi*f*(t-tcenter))+b*sin(2*pi*f*(t-tcenter)) on ALL original retained samples. No resampling, Hann weighting, filtering, outlier removal, or nominal-target constraint. The search is centered on the largest native FFT bin with configured halfwidth in native bins; a coarse frequency grid selects a local bracket for bounded refinement. Frequency is unavailable on a rejected fit; candidate diagnostics retained.
methods.sine_amplitude: sqrt(a*a+b*b), a fitted sinusoidal peak amplitude in original signal units, distinct from FFT peak amplitude and raw RMS/peak-to-peak. Offset fitted jointly. Residual RMS includes model mismatch, harmonics and noise; it is not a measured noise floor or SNR. No calibrated uncertainty inferred.
methods.time_assumption: Raw timestamp fit conditionally treats recorded Time_us as acquisition times. That relationship is not documented; receive/logging timestamps need not be accurate sample times. Agreement with FFT does not calibrate a shared timebase or prove generator frequency.
methods.strict_view: The same existing strict-gap eligibility mask is applied to every estimator only to compare a common subset; nonuniform-time sine fitting does not intrinsically require uniform intervals.
methods.comparison_aggregation: Each record/window remains separate. Frequency error means estimate minus nominal setting, not independently measured truth; ppm=1e6*(estimate-target)/target. Group means and sample SD use independent records only; 90s and 100s windows are not repeats. Mean offsets/ppm are descriptive and are never subtracted as a calibration.
methods.reference: For each sensor/base_hz/window_variant/method, use the mean of finite estimates at target_hz equal to base_hz (absolute tolerance 1e-9 Hz, zero relative tolerance). Missing finite baseline leaves relative estimates unavailable; no reference fallback.
methods.relative_record: 1000*(estimate_hz-baseline_mean_hz), in mHz. All original estimates, statuses and timestamp quality flags are retained. Reference subtraction is a display/summary convention, not a frequency or timebase calibration.
methods.group_scatter: Means and sample SD (ddof=1) use finite independent-file estimates for one target/method/window. SD is unavailable for fewer than two estimates. SD bars describe record scatter, not a confidence interval or propagated uncertainty in the baseline-referenced mean. Baseline SD and SEM remain explicit in CSV outputs.
methods.nominal_bias: nominal_error_ppm=1e6*(estimate_hz-target_hz)/target_hz; target_hz is a nominal setting, not calibrated truth. Group ppm mean and sample SD are computed without baseline subtraction. Zero nominal target has unavailable ppm.
methods.replicates: One row per sensor/file/window/method, with duplicate identities rejected. Window variants are summarized separately and never treated as independent records. No exclusions are introduced by this summary; original estimator/quality statuses remain available.

volume_reference_methods.pairing: Explicit configured file pairs, joined by amplifier volume setting only; separate acquisitions.
volume_reference_methods.amplitude: Global positive-frequency padded FFT maximum refined using its two neighboring bins; original spectrum preprocessing retained.
volume_reference_methods.normalization: Each sensor amplitude divided by its own amplitude at the configured reference volume; no cross-sensor unit conversion.
volume_reference_methods.ratio: IM Data28 peak amplitude / accelerometer peak acceleration in g (nominal per-record full-scale conversion); descriptive conditional proxy, not calibrated sensitivity.
volume_reference_methods.ratio_usable: A numerical comparison with confirmed matching conditions, one row per sensor and volume, finite positive amplitudes, computed FFTs, matching nominal frequency, compatible global peaks, and accelerometer extrema occupancy below threshold. Timestamp-warning estimates remain diagnostic.
volume_reference_methods.plateau_flag: Fraction of retained raw accelerometer samples equal to the observed minimum OR maximum >= configured threshold; diagnostic repeated-extrema flag, not proof of sensor saturation.
volume_reference_methods.limits: Sequential acquisitions may differ because of drift; no synchronized transfer function, phase, coherence, or time/pulse pairing. No calibration or regression inferred.

snr_methods.metric: Nominal-band excess-power SNR against each separate noise recording; supplemental to global FFT peak estimates, which are unchanged.
snr_methods.signal_estimator: Integrate the native one-sided periodic-Hann periodogram PSD of each excited analysis window over the configured nominal-frequency band. Estimated excess power = measured excited band power minus reference noise band power. This is band excess, not an isolated fundamental estimator.
snr_methods.noise_estimator: Welch PSD on each explicitly configured same-sensor control separately: default 6 s periodic Hann, 50% overlap, per-segment constant detrend, nfft=nperseg, arithmetic mean in linear PSD. Requested nperseg is never silently shortened. No averaging between control recordings.
snr_methods.preprocessing: Use the existing fixed-N linear timestamp interpolation and fs=(N-1)/retained span. Excited periodogram removes its window mean; Welch removes each segment mean. No additional bandpass or other filter, accel uses the same nominal counts-to-g conversion for signal and noise when enabled; no zero padding for PSD integration.
snr_methods.bandwidth: Default nominal target +/-1 Hz, clipped to common represented PSD frequency support. Integrate piecewise-linear PSD using trapezoids with interpolated values at identical physical band edges for signal and noise. Retain the DC endpoint after detrending; no original DC level is added. Common support ends at min(last positive excited bin,last noise bin), at or just below Nyquist. Report exact edges, width, df, ENBW, and clipping.
snr_methods.linear_and_db: SNR_power=(P_excited-P_noise)/P_noise; SNR_dB=10*log10(SNR_power) only for positive finite noise and positive excess. Nonpositive excess remains recorded, while its SNR_dB and SNR_power are NaN, never floored. Independently retain measured band-power ratio P_excited/P_noise and 10*log10 of that ratio; zero measured power gives -inf, not an invented floor.
snr_methods.assumptions: Subtraction assumes the separate control represents the background during excitation and background/excitation powers add without coherent cross terms. These are unverified conditions, not synchronization. IM_1 nothing-on comparison includes any amplifier-added power; IM_2 amplifier-on is a separate reference. Other components and fixed lines inside the band contribute, including interference around 200 Hz. Results do not establish fundamental detection, detection limit, calibrated sensitivity, or physical frequency response.
snr_methods.aggregation_and_quality: One value per excited window and each configured control; no averaging of targets or reference recordings, no confidence interval from overlapping Welch segments. Retain both records' actual windows, time-gap eligibility, flags and PSD settings. Unavailable, ambiguous, wrong-sensor and undersupported references stay flagged with missing values. Computational availability does not imply calibrated validity.

accel_config.basis: ASM330LHH nominal sensitivity by recording full scale

limitations: Original-time sine fitting assumes Time_us represents acquisition instants; the timestamp source is unconfirmed. A good fit cannot independently calibrate timestamp scale or excitation frequency. The stationary single-sine model can be affected by harmonics/drift, and residual RMS is not a measured noise floor.

Five-point quadratic fits are not guaranteed more accurate than three-point fits. Native Hann outer bins can approach main-lobe zeros and bias log-domain frequency/amplitude fits; padded bins span a narrower interval. Neither fit point count nor padding increases physical resolving power.

Nominal-band SNR uses independent noise controls; it depends on bandwidth and background representativeness. Amplifier-added noise contributes relative to the nothing-on control. Interference in the band is included; excess power is not proof of a detected sine fundamental.
Start offsets and transition times are configured assumptions until verified against experiment notes; nominal dwell durations do not establish actual switching times.
Global maximum can be interference or a harmonic; neither a small frequency error nor a large peak establishes detection or calibrated bandwidth.

Computed FFTs with internal gap warnings are diagnostics; strict-gap results are retained separately. Neither view establishes clock accuracy. Timestamp jitter, gaps, interpolation, finite window length and low samples/cycle can bias frequency/amplitude; analog sensor/logger/drive bandwidth and clock accuracy remain uncalibrated.
Generator 1 Vpp and amplifier volume are settings, not measured physical input. IM amplitudes remain Data28 counts; accel amplitudes use nominally converted g.

Repeat counts follow effective user-specified FILES and are saved separately. Sample SD uses only settings with at least two finite independent-record estimates; small n does not establish a resolution limit.
